_about: Why each class and relation exists, and who confirmed it. Written by the ontology interview and edited by hand. `validated_by` is empty until a person who knows the domain has actually confirmed the entry; leave it empty rather than guessing.

ActionItem.question: What did we commit to, and is it done?
ActionItem.why: A commitment has an owner and a lifecycle state, and it is what turns a decision into work.

Concept.alternatives: Deliberately broad for a first draft. Split it as soon as the sub-kinds are nameable.
Concept.question: What are we designing or adopting, and what does it mean here?
Concept.why: New vocabulary is the main output of a transformation, and every stakeholder needs one definition of it.

Decision.alternatives: Considered a status field; rejected because a status keeps neither reason nor history.
Decision.question: What did we settle, when, and why?
Decision.why: A decision carries a reason and a date, and a later one supersedes it rather than erasing it.

Deliverable.question: What did we contract to produce, and is it accepted?
Deliverable.why: A deliverable has a due date and an acceptance condition, which are commitments rather than descriptions.

Document.question: Where is this written down?
Document.why: Every fact needs a checkable source with its own date.

Engagement.question: What is in scope, for whom, over what period?
Engagement.why: The engagement bounds everything else, and its period is what makes a fact current or historical.

Framework.question: What method are we applying, and where did it come from?
Framework.why: A method brought in from outside is not the engagement's own design, and the distinction matters for provenance.

GovernanceForum.alternatives: Considered treating each meeting as the forum; rejected because it cannot answer what this board has decided.
GovernanceForum.question: Which body decides this, and what has it decided?
GovernanceForum.why: A forum recurs and accumulates decisions, so it must persist independently of any single meeting.

Organization.alternatives: Considered separate Client and Supplier classes; rejected because units nest inside both.
Organization.question: Who is the client, who is the supplier, and which unit is affected?
Organization.why: Both sides and their internal units have to be referenceable, and the same class serves all three.

Person.alternatives: Strongly considered omitting entirely. The engagement this came from added a roster of several hundred named employees and had to purge it from repository history.
Person.question: Whose individual decision was this?
Person.why: Kept only for the few people whose decisions must be traced. Most ownership questions are answered better by a role.

Question.question: What is still open, and who owns getting the answer?
Question.why: Open questions are the most perishable knowledge in an engagement and the first thing lost when people rotate.

Role.question: Who is accountable, without naming a person?
Role.why: Roles are stable while people move, so attaching ownership to a role keeps history correct.

Session.alternatives: Considered merging with Document; rejected because one session can be recorded in several files and vice versa.
Session.question: What happened on that date, and what came out of it?
Session.why: A session is a dated event with outcomes, and it is separate from any document recording it.

Workstream.question: Which part of the engagement is this, and who runs it?
Workstream.why: Work is planned and reported per workstream, and each has its own owner and its own deliverables.

instance_of.question: What has this board actually decided?
instance_of.why: Linking a session to its recurring forum is what makes the whole history of a governance body queryable.

part_of.alternatives: This is the relation whose declared domain and range drifted most on the source engagement. Keep it honest or split it.
part_of.question: What sits inside what?
part_of.why: One containment relation across units, workstreams and concepts keeps traversal simple, at the cost of a wide domain.
